title: The board comes down
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Labor Day. The last of the summer boats. Gully takes OPEN DAILY down and hangs it inside on a nail for next year. The uncle says nobody came daily. Gully says some did. The uncle says name one. Gully says the dog.

panels.composition: The launch, Labor Day, the last trailers pulling out. GULLY unhooking the OPEN DAILY board. The UNCLE in the chair. WOOD, BARNABY.

image.prompt: a boat launch on a holiday with the last trailers leaving, a teenager taking a hand-painted board down from a shack wall, an old man in a lawn chair, a young man and a dog, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The board going onto a nail inside, above the walrus.

image.prompt: close on a hand-painted board being hung on a nail inside a shack above a small framed drawing, black and white, no words
an old man in a lawn chair, flat, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The shack with one sign again. The dog on the step. The uncle looking at the dog. Conceding, the way he does: not at all, out loud.

image.prompt: a shingle shack with a single sign, a small dog on its step and an old man in a lawn chair looking at the dog, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'Name one.' 'The dog.' The board waits inside for next summer.
